STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel has a flat centre and a rim band with no visible inner wall, rounded-square outline. Flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are 20-30 cm; the plate looks medium-sized, around 22-24 cm.
b) Reference cue: grapes/cherry tomatoes are about 2.2-3 cm. The plate spans roughly 9-10 tomato-widths across the visible width (about 340 px plate width, tomatoes about 35-40 px each), giving about 9 x 3 cm ≈ 25-27 cm. Hmm, using grape scale (~2.2 cm, about 25 px) gives about 13 grapes across ≈ 29 cm, but the tomatoes are the larger reference and are more reliable here.
Reconcile: width ≈ 24 cm (square, area ≈ 576 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Red cherry/grape tomatoes: visible count ≈ 14. Hidden underneath (pile about 2 deep at the centre): add about 4, total ≈ 18. Grams = 18 x 15 = 270 g. Note these are sized like cherry tomatoes (~3 cm), so 15 g each is reasonable.
- Green grape: 1 visible, 5 g.
- Small sauce/juice smear and bits: negligible; a few grams, ignore beyond a rounding allowance.

Check the footprint method for consistency: the food cluster covers about 15% of the plate (~86 cm²), with a pile about 2 pieces (~5 cm) thick at the centre, average ~2.5 cm. Volume ≈ 215 ml x 0.6 density ≈ 130 g. The count-based estimate (270 g) is higher because cherry tomatoes are hollow-packed and some are hidden; I trust the count more but settle at a midpoint of about 200 g for the red tomatoes.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer visible; the plate is essentially flat, so no hidden base beyond the tomato stacking already counted.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Cherry tomatoes: about 18 kcal/100 g.
- Grapes (green): about 69 kcal/100 g.

Totals: red tomatoes ≈ 200 g (≈36 kcal); green grape ≈ 5 g (≈3.5 kcal). Total ≈ 205 g, ≈40 kcal.
